target_function: Primer pore electrostatic guide & lateral wall
atomic_mechanism: Removes basic pore charge (5.75 A to DNA DT 12:OP1) and lateral packing against Tyr176:O (3.65 A). Destroys secondary kinetic retention during translocation without touching RNA template A55.
Arginine maintains aliphatic CD packing against Tyr176:O while providing terminal guanidinium positive charge in the exit pore. Decisive positive control restoring TPP1 processivity transmission.
Abolishes the 2.338 A H-bond to Gln794:OE1, pi-pi sandwich with Phe759 (3.41 A), and packing with Lys757:CD (3.65 A). Decouples inter-domain dynamic damping between TEN and TRAP.
Preserves aromatic ring packing against Phe759 and Lys757 while removing hydroxyl; isolates energetic contribution of the Gln794 hydrogen bond.
Retains positive charge at 756 but lacks planar guanidinium ring. Demonstrates that planar pi-stacking with A55 is essential for basal template translocation.
Heavily confounded by direct loss of A55 pi-stacking. Unsuitable as sole decoupling proof due to intrinsic catalytic defect.
Abolishes the 3.58 A salt bridge to TPP1 Glu215. Diagnostic control proving that disrupting the TEN recruitment lobe abolishes RAP via loss of affinity.
Abolishes the 2.32 A salt bridge to TPP1 Glu168. Diagnostic control proving that disrupting the TRAP recruitment lobe abolishes RAP via loss of affinity.
Disrupts 3.67 A hydrophobic packing with TPP1 Leu183. Recruitment-defective control.
Probes the canonical TEN anchor site for long DNA primers. Tests whether TPP1 RAP stimulation requires distal anchor binding.
Hairpin stem solvent-exposed residue. Negative control proving that arbitrary alanine substitutions in the TRAP stem do not impair allosteric signaling.
Stem hydrophobic core residue. Negative control demonstrating structural tolerance.
